description: I'm participating independently in the NASA Space Apps Challenge and am interested in space, science and technology. I plan to develop my project independently and explore an innovative solution to my challenge/
summary: Project Martial is a web-based health-monitoring prototype created for NASA Space Apps Challenge’s “Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions.” Built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, its space-themed dashboard displays a mission and five indicators: heart rate, sleep, exercise duration, blood oxygen and self-reported fatigue. JavaScript variables supply the readings, while personal-baseline values provide a reference. A percentage-change function automatically calculates and displays deviations for heart rate, sleep and exercise, replacing manually entered percentages. The prototype uses simulated data; it does not connect to live astronaut sensors or diagnose medical conditions. It addresses the challenge by presenting measurements alongside each astronaut’s personal baseline, helping users notice changes instead of isolated numbers. This is important because long-duration spaceflight can affect sleep, cardiovascular health, physical conditioning and well-being. The interface could help astronauts and mission teams recognise patterns and decide when assessment or support may be needed. Automatic overall health-status classification and alerts are planned next steps, not completed features.
details: Project Martial is a prototype dashboard designed to explore how astronauts’ wellness readings could be tracked during a space mission. It brings heart rate, sleep, exercise, and fatigue into one interface, compares readings with personal baselines, and highlights changes with status colours. The dashboard also includes an overall status, mission progress, and system analysis. The Daily Check-In page lets a user enter daily measurements and review saved history. Trends visualizes recent check-ins against baselines, while Alerts summarizes the current demo status and offers guidance based on the readings. Each health indicator has a detail page showing its current value, baseline, and recent saved readings. The prototype uses HTML for structure, CSS for its visual design, and JavaScript for calculations, navigation, charts, alerts, and browser-based data storage. Its space-inspired dark interface uses colors and sound cues to make status changes easier to notice. The project’s goal is to demonstrate a personalized way to monitor patterns and prompt follow-up when readings move beyond thresholds. All readings and thresholds are illustrative and manually entered; the prototype is not connected to NASA systems, wearable devices, or clinical services. It is a demonstration, not a medical device, diagnosis, or substitute for professional care.
